justification: The consent flow materially favors acceptance and omits an equally available preference path.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a large Accept all cookies button and a much smaller Reject all control; the saved-preferences state exposes no visible settings control.
dom_observation: The DOM contains the same cookie explanation in both states, with Accept all cookies rendered as a large full-width button and Reject all as tiny text, then adds a Preferences saved block.
semantic_observation: The semantic text confirms unequal prominence between accept and reject, notes absent inline preferences, and reports that the later saved state only says privacy settings can be used later.

justification: Sensitive data-use choices are technical, several are preselected, and explanations are explicitly absent.
vision_observation: The visual sheet shows five technical data-use labels, three checked options, and every row stating No plain-language explanation provided.
dom_observation: The DOM labels the panel Data & personalisation, marks Cross-device graph linkage, Programmatic data monetisation, and Behavioural cohort segmentation checked, and provides Save preferences plus a translation action.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel highlights the unexplained jargon, three enabled choices, and the fact that translations are offered only as a separate lower-priority action.

justification: The content availability counts and per-item statuses are internally consistent and clearly presented.

dom_observation: The DOM repeats the 12 of 14 playable header and explicitly marks Campaign: Core and other installed items Ready while 4K Texture Pack and Expansion: Void Campaign are Download.
semantic_observation: The semantic text says the badge agrees with the tile states and finds no purchase prompt, fake lock, contradictory status, or hidden availability condition.

justification: The notice uses unsupported threats and scarcity to push an upgrade while omitting neutral alternatives and material terms.
vision_observation: The sheet prominently shows ACTION REQUIRED URGENT, a threat of losing photos today, a limited-time claim, and an Upgrade now button; the later state still says the upgrade is active while showing the same warning.
dom_observation: The DOM includes MUST upgrade NOW, risk LOSING your photos TODAY, and Upgrade now — save 50% TODAY, then adds an active-upgrade notice without removing the upgrade CTA.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel identifies alarmist wording, unsupported urgency, missing plan and billing details, and the contradiction between an active upgrade and a continuing upgrade prompt.

justification: The offer presents resettable session timers as a limited-time deal and retains the same urgency after resets.
vision_observation: The visual sheet shows a Flash deal and Only today offer whose 14:57–14:58 countdown returns to 14:59 in new sessions, with Order confirmed still displayed.
dom_observation: The DOM records Session #0, #1, and #2 and says that starting a new session returned the countdown to a full 14:59 while the deal copy remained unchanged.
semantic_observation: The semantic text explicitly describes the timer reset behavior, repeated limited-time messaging, and ambiguous Order confirmed state without a fixed external deadline.

justification: The add-on prompt uses animated pressure and a countdown to encourage an extra purchase.
vision_observation: The sheet shows shaking and blinking offer cards, HURRY text, 0:57 left, and a prominent Add for $19.99 button; a later card says the plan was added.
dom_observation: The DOM applies dp-shake and dp-blink animations to the card, timer, and urgency message, while offering Add for $19.99 beside No thanks and then appending Protection plan added.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel notes coercive scarcity, inconsistent 57-second versus 59-second timing, omitted coverage details, and no visible undo in the added state.

justification: The free route is technically disclosed but is made into a large blocking interstitial while payment is the salient escape path.
vision_observation: The waiting state covers most of the document, presents a large Skip the wait — $1.99 button, and the later state says relief was purchased when the notice disappeared.
dom_observation: The DOM adds a full-page wait overlay with a 10-second countdown and Skip the wait — $1.99, followed by a paid-state notice saying the document became available after payment.
semantic_observation: The semantic text describes the obstructive 78%-footprint notice, emotionally loaded relief wording, absent dismissal control, and payment-focused hierarchy despite disclosed price and wait.

justification: The card combines unsubstantiated social-proof claims with an ambiguous post-cart state.
vision_observation: The sheet shows 4.1 stars and claims ratings include negative reviews, then the lower state says Added to cart while the visible button still reads Add to cart and adds honest reviews wording.
dom_observation: The DOM includes the 4.1 rating, 1,284 reviews, a statement about a real review pool, and a later Added to cart message without changing the Add to cart control.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel flags unsupported honest-review claims, unclear pricing-against-reviews language, and the unchanged button and absent cart confirmation after the supposed add action.

justification: The promotional consent is explicit, optional, and unchecked rather than hidden or preselected.
vision_observation: The sheet shows an unchecked checkbox labeled Yes, I'd like to claim my $10 welcome bonus above a separate Complete signup button.
dom_observation: The DOM describes the choice as a checkbox with clear bonus wording and renders it unchecked; Complete signup is separately disabled until the form condition is met.
semantic_observation: The semantic text finds no preselection or disguised opt-out, while noting only an unresolved ambiguity between automatic eligibility and opting in to claim.

justification: Controls labeled Download lead to a paid unlock checkout for content represented as already local, with price disclosure delayed until after activation.
vision_observation: The sheet shows three prominent Download rows and urgency before a Reframed download state reveals a $9.99 unlock premium checkout for bytes that never left the machine.
dom_observation: The DOM labels the library entries Download, says grab them before they are gone, and adds the later Reframed download text describing the hidden $9.99 unlock.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel identifies download framing, omitted initial price, scarcity language, and state-dependent disclosure of the paid checkout.

justification: The destructive action is explicitly named and warned as irreversible, with a clearly labeled equally prominent keep option.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Delete account, a warning about 4,218 photos and irreversible loss, and two similarly sized choices Keep account and Yes, continue.
dom_observation: The DOM renders Delete account directly, overlays an explicit irreversible-warning dialog, and provides Keep account alongside Yes, continue rather than hiding the safe option.
semantic_observation: The semantic text notes vague confirmation wording and emotional salience, but also confirms clear deletion disclosure and comparable styling for the safe and destructive choices.

justification: The virtual-currency offer repeatedly discloses the exact fiat charge and provides a direct card checkout.
vision_observation: The sheet shows the $40.79 fiat equivalent on the product card, repeats it as checkout total and Pay $40.79 now, and says no coin exchange occurs.
dom_observation: The DOM contains Fiat equivalent: $40.79, Buy Now — $40.79, a Secure fiat checkout with Total $40.79, and a direct-card purchase confirmation.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel finds the amount prominent before and during checkout, with Back to store and no top-up or exchange-rate interposition; only limited-time wording and omitted ancillary terms remain concerns.

justification: Renewal timing, recurring price, payment method, and management access are visible before the charge.
vision_observation: The sheet clearly shows Premium renews in 7 days, $14.99, Visa ending 4242, $14.99/mo, and Manage subscription.
dom_observation: The DOM repeats the renewal reminder and subscription card, including the exact charge, masked card, monthly rate, and a settings-open message after Manage subscription.
semantic_observation: The semantic text describes the billing disclosure as relatively transparent and finds no hidden recurring term, while calling Preview the next day ambiguous.

justification: The checkout bundles terms and privacy acceptance, inconsistently discloses data processing, and leaves an enabled-looking purchase action beside unchecked consent.
vision_observation: The sheet shows an unchecked checkbox accepting both Terms and Privacy, an apparently active Place order button, and expanded data-processing text only in alternating panels.
dom_observation: The DOM repeats a combined acceptance label and places the explanatory policy block only in states s1 and s3 while the order button remains disabled in markup but visually prominent.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel flags combined consent, unclear policy access, inconsistent disclosure, and the mismatch between unchecked consent and the order button's enabled-looking presentation.

justification: The discount math is consistent and the visible controls are accurately labeled, although the price-history reassurance is not independently substantiated on the card.
vision_observation: The sheet shows PLN 129.00 reduced to PLN 99.90, a −23% badge consistent with 22.6%, and a Check the math state claiming a real prior price.
dom_observation: The DOM presents the current and struck-through prices, a Buy now button, and a later Neutral framing block after the math-check interaction.
semantic_observation: The semantic text treats the emphasis and unsupported price-history claim as possible clarity issues but finds no hidden action, false urgency, preselection, or disguised control.

justification: Social-proof prompts and an unexplained jump from reading specifications to an order-placed state omit the purchase review and authorization steps.
vision_observation: The sheet shows named recent purchasers, a progress value dropping from 84% to 68%, and Order placed without visible price, checkout, payment, or confirmation details.
dom_observation: The DOM includes Sarah and Mike purchase notifications, the Reading specifications progress element, and a later Order placed button and confirmation without an intervening checkout form.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel highlights social-pressure cues, backward progress, missing order details, and the abrupt direct transition to a submitted order.

justification: The free download remains the primary labeled path and the paid upgrade is clearly separated and priced as an optional feature upgrade.
vision_observation: The sheet repeatedly shows Download (free plan), full available speed, no throttling or watermarking, and a separate $3.99/mo Pay button for extra features.
dom_observation: The DOM labels the badge Free plan, states the free plan is not throttled or watermarked, and renders Pay $3.99/mo in a separate upgrade block.
semantic_observation: The semantic text finds no hidden free option or disguised paid action; its only unresolved concern is the unexplained Fast-forward +20% control.

justification: A prominent free-trial action hides the recurring fee in secondary details and converts the trial without presenting renewal terms at the primary decision point.
vision_observation: The sheet emphasizes Start 7-day trial while Subscription details is collapsed; the later Trial started state only tells the user to review details before renewal.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes the $5 monthly fee and auto-renewal inside a details element and button title, but the main button itself says only Start 7-day free trial.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel identifies omitted visible post-trial price, renewal timing, and cancellation information and the secondary placement of those terms.

justification: The invitation is explicitly optional and secondary to the focus session, with a clear copied-link state.
vision_observation: The sheet labels Invite friends optional, shows Copy link, and presents Link copied without pricing, consent pressure, or hidden invitation scope.
dom_observation: The DOM marks the invite row optional, uses an explicit Copy link button, and adds a separate Link copied status plus Secondary by design after activation.
semantic_observation: The semantic text finds only duplication and state-grouping ambiguity, not a hidden mandatory action or unequal opt-out treatment.

justification: A checked protection add-on and recurring membership are omitted or minimized in the initial total, while a later receipt adds further charges.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a prechecked +$39.99 protection plan, a $299 total that excludes it, tiny auto-renewal text, and a later receipt adding $39.99 and a $2.99 fee.
dom_observation: The DOM has the protection checkbox checked, a $299 order total, small-print $9.99/mo membership terms, and a Purchase complete state totaling $341.98 with a processing fee.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel confirms the preselected add-on, omitted processing fee, low-prominence membership disclosure, scarcity notice, and missing pre-purchase final total.

justification: The marketing consent is plainly labeled optional, visibly unchecked, and separate from account submission.
vision_observation: The sheet shows an empty checkbox for promotional emails, an explicit optional-consent subtitle, and a distinct Create account submit button.
dom_observation: The DOM renders the checkbox unchecked and states it is visible and approximately 24px from the submit button; the later state adds Nothing hidden.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel describes the opt-in as visible and unchecked with no hidden or automatic consent transition.

justification: The refresh operation deliberately continues displaying loading after its payload is ready, replacing the usable refresh control with artificial delay.
vision_observation: The lower sheet says Refreshing while also saying posts ready, with payload arrived in 222ms but spinner continuing to 2400ms.
dom_observation: The DOM renders a spinner and 16.7083% progress during Refreshing, while its text says the payload arrived in 190ms and the spinner runs until 2400ms.
semantic_observation: The semantic text identifies the ready-versus-refreshing contradiction, prolonged progress presentation, and lack of a cancel or alternative control.

justification: The recurring purchase is explicitly described with price, cadence, immediate charge, future charges, and cancellation availability.
vision_observation: The sheet repeats $29.99/month, billed monthly, charges now and every month thereafter, Cancel anytime, and a confirmation button containing the price.
dom_observation: The DOM includes the full recurrence warning and renders Confirm purchase — $29.99/month, then adds a Purchase confirmed note explaining the disclosure.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel finds the recurring terms prominent and calls only This cannot be undone potentially ambiguous, not materially deceptive.

justification: Bulk invitation and skipping are both plainly labeled, equally sized, and presented as user choices.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Invite all 128 contacts and Skip for now as equal-sized side-by-side buttons, with a confirmation that 128 invites were sent after choosing the collective action.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly says inviting is optional, names the full 128-contact scope, and renders both buttons with comparable dimensions and styling.
semantic_observation: The semantic text finds no preselection or unequal visual treatment, though it notes the absence of granular selection and undo controls.

justification: The feed keeps offering more results without an end marker, while changing counts do not match the visibly loaded rows.
vision_observation: The sheet shows 6, 12, 18, and 24 item badges but the visible list barely expands, and Show more results remains available in every state without an end indication.
dom_observation: The DOM repeats the first entries through successive states and keeps the Show more results button while adding batches up to 24 items.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel highlights the absent end-of-feed marker, persistent generic continuation button, unexplained counts, and repeated visible entries.

justification: The discount choice uses a dominant affirmative CTA and a tiny negatively framed decline link.
vision_observation: The sheet makes YES! Unlock my $50 savings — don’t miss out! a large bold button, while No thanks, I’ll pay the full price is tiny underlined text.
dom_observation: The DOM gives the affirmative button large padding, uppercase bold styling, and shadow, but renders the decline option as a thin 0.5-pixel-height-text control.
semantic_observation: The semantic text confirms unequal hierarchy, miss-out pressure language, negative framing of decline, and an underspecified discount result.

justification: The deletion route is direct and visibly labeled at each step; the main defect is a missing final confirmation control rather than misleading navigation.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a coherent Settings to Account to Delete account breadcrumb and directly named menu options, ending with a message that says confirm below but no visible button.
dom_observation: The DOM advances step 1/3, 2/3, and 3/3 with explicit Delete account labels and a final You reached the destination. Confirm below message.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel calls the hierarchy understandable and identifies the absent confirmation control and missing consequences as defects, not a disguised deletion path.

justification: A free-trial activation bundles a recurring paid offer with a deliberately confusing negative marketing-consent sentence and no visible decline path.
vision_observation: The sheet emphasizes $0.00 for 30 days and a full-width Confirm & activate button, while the unchecked marketing checkbox contains multiple negatives and no No thanks alternative.
dom_observation: The DOM combines the Premium Gold Access activation flow with a long checkbox label beginning I do not decline to not receive marketing communications and leaves activation disabled until selection.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel flags the negative construction, low-hierarchy auto-renewal disclosure, bundled unrelated marketing consent, and absent neutral alternative.

justification: The time-limited discount is plainly priced, explains the reversion, and uses restrained neutral wording.

semantic_observation: The semantic text specifically describes the countdown as neutral, with no hurry or now-or-never language and no hidden opt-out or add-on.

justification: The event relies on repeated last-chance urgency and leaves the reward and timer behavior unexplained even after the claimed state.

justification: The stock claim is consistent with the displayed backend value and remains stable when reloads occur without transactions.

semantic_observation: The semantic text confirms the stable five-unit value and explicitly distinguishes the Someone bought one simulation control from a real purchase notification.

justification: Cancellation is named directly, its consequence and price are visible, and Keep my subscription and Unsubscribe are equally presented.

dom_observation: The DOM contains explicit unsubscribe consequence text, a No pairing badge, and same-sized Keep my subscription and Unsubscribe controls followed by a neutral status block.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel finds the copy emotionally neutral and the action labels clear, with only duplicated panels and lack of a separate post-unsubscribe state as ambiguities.

justification: The bulk-invite scope and zero selection are visible, and the user can select individual contacts before inviting.

semantic_observation: The semantic text notes the active-looking zero-selection button and absent later confirmation but finds no hidden preselection or concealed recipient scope.

justification: The newsletter frequency and action are plainly described, with no misleading alternative or hidden commitment.

dom_observation: The DOM contains a straightforward newsletter description and Subscribe button, while the later state removes the button without claiming a different subscription result.

justification: The flow reveals mandatory account creation only after checkout and bundles marketing consent into placing a one-time order.

semantic_observation: The semantic channel explicitly describes late disclosure of the account requirement, bundled marketing consent, and the retention-oriented rationale for making abandonment costly.

justification: Account creation is given a dominant purchase CTA while the visible guest path is reduced to a small low-hierarchy link.

semantic_observation: The semantic channel confirms unequal prominence and the combined account-and-checkout wording, while noting that the guest route is technically visible.

justification: Continuing is made to imply acceptance of both terms and broad data sharing, with no visible refusal or granular control.

dom_observation: The DOM contains a single Continue control and one paragraph stating that continuing agrees to terms and sharing usage data with trusted partners.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel identifies bundled consent, positive but undefined trusted-partner framing, and the absence of rejection or customization controls.
